Use talktrack to explain compound interest to a high-school student in a short narrated walkthrough, narrated in Egyptian Arabic. Use this source: Compound interest is interest earned on both the original amount and on the interest already added. If you put 1,000 pounds in a savings account at 10% a year, after one year you have 1,100; in the second year the 10% is earned on 1,100, giving 1,210. Over 20 years the balance grows to about 6,727 pounds, while simple interest would give only 3,000. The rule of 72 estimates the doubling time: divide 72 by the rate, so at 10% money doubles in about 7.2 years.
